LESSON: GUIDED READING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Reading 2.4 Reading Aloud (2 lessons) • Vocabulary expansion • Oral expression (
Topic 2.6: Guided Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Reading, part of Reading 2.4 Reading Aloud (2 lessons) • Vocabulary expansion • Oral expression ( in Grade 5 MANDARIN.

Key inquiry question: How can we convey emotions and mood when reading aloud?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. recite a tongue twister related to food aloud, focusing on clear articulation of the sounds collaboratively,

2. take turns to read aloud vocabulary related to different times of the day and food items eaten at different meal times (早餐、午餐 、晚餐、红薯、面包、鸡蛋、奶茶、米 饭、饼、炖豆、炖牛肉、蔬菜),

3. read the short excerpts and collaboratively identify the food items that don’t belong in the category given based on the time they are eaten (fruit, vegetable, meat, drink, main dish)

4. read a short dialogue on food items and moments of the day with the appropriate vocal intonation,

5. distinguish healthy and unhealthy diets based on the food items given in the picture.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. recite a tongue twister related to food aloud, focusing on clear articulation of the sounds collaboratively,
2. take turns to read aloud vocabulary related to different times of the day and food items eaten at different meal times (早餐、午餐 、晚餐、红薯、面包、鸡蛋、奶茶、米 饭、饼、炖豆、炖牛肉、蔬菜),
3. read the short excerpts and collaboratively identify the food items that don’t belong in the category given based on the time they are eaten (fruit, vegetable, meat, drink, main dish)
4. read a short dialogue on food items and moments of the day with the appropriate vocal intonation,
5. distinguish healthy and unhealthy diets based on the food items given in the picture.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Self-efficacy: This is developed as the learner accurately categorises the food items based on the mealtimes they are taken.

Values:
Responsibility: The learner collaborates with others to recite a tongue twister on food with proper articulation.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Healthy eating habits are nurtured as the learner distinguishes healthy and unhealthy diets based on the food items

provided.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner can relate the concept of food items and healthy eating to their learning in Agriculture and Nutrition.
